question: _________ oblong orbit overlaps the orbit of Neptune.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Pluto's**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pluto's** oblong orbit overlaps the orbit of Neptune.
 
• Pluto is classified as a dwarf planet in the Kuiper belt, a ring of bodies beyond Neptune.
 
• The orbit of Pluto is highly elliptical, taking it inside the orbit of Neptune for 20 years of its 248-year orbit around the Sun.
 
• This unique orbital characteristic means that at certain times, Pluto is closer to the Sun than Neptune.
 
• Despite this overlap, there is no risk of collision due to their respective orbital inclinations and resonance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pluto** was discovered by Clyde Tombaugh in 1930 and was originally classified as the ninth planet of the Solar System.
 
• In 2006, the International Astronomical Union (IAU) redefined the criteria for planet classification, and Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet.
 
• Pluto has five known moons: Charon, Styx, Nix, Kerberos, and Hydra.
 
• The New Horizons mission, launched by NASA, performed a flyby of Pluto in 2015, providing the most detailed images and data of the dwarf planet to date.
 
• Pluto's surface is composed of a mixture of frozen nitrogen, methane, and carbon monoxide ices.
 
• It has a thin atmosphere that expands when it is closer to the Sun and collapses as it moves farther away.
